problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=2{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+3t-2,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t),\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)) \\  & =2t\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+t\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+2t\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+3 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t) & =-3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(t) & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ t & ={e}^{-3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t={e}^{-3/2}.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}v({e}^{-3/2}) & =2({e}^{-3/2})\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-3/2})+{e}^{-3/2} \\  & =2{e}^{-3/2}(-\frac{3}{2})+{e}^{-3/2} \\  & =-2{e}^{-3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$
